routines.semantics: Returns and consumes the agent update notification. Registration and writes to watched variables set the flag; unrelated writes do not. Different agents consume independently, and an unregistered agent returns false. kclear affects the pool but registered watches are part of CSPICE process/module state.

scenarios.observes: Each actual returned boolean reaches comparison across registration, consumption, unrelated writes, per-agent independent notifications, additive registration and an unregistered agent. Case: cvpool reports the expected update flags before and after a tracked variable change

routines.edgeAssessment: Returns and consumes the agent update notification. Registration and writes to watched variables set the flag; unrelated writes do not. Different agents consume independently, and an unregistered agent returns false. kclear affects the pool but registered watches are part of CSPICE process/module state. routines.errorAssessment: Blank identifiers and invalid paging are contract/wrapper validation, not raw CSPICE diagnostic parity. Actual BADVARNAME writes and INTOUTOFRANGE integer conversion are named live errors where applicable. Missing/wrong-type lookups are successful Found/boolean outcomes. Pool/agent exhaustion would require disruptive global-capacity stress rather than a small deterministic semantic fixture; allocation rollback is separately fault-injected at all 43 temporary allocation positions. Null C pointers and undersized output buffers are not reachable through valid typed adapters.
routines.fixtureRationale: No external fixtures or kernels. Distinguishing numeric arrays, ASCII strings, short case-sensitive variable/agent names, and a deliberately overlong variable name are authored in the scenarios; no scientific data or distribution issue.
routines.cleanup: Both workflow runtimes clear the pool around each case and reset error state. CSPICE watch registrations can outlive kclear, so watched names/agents are deterministically reused in self-contained workflows and re-armed/consumed rather than assumed absent; unregistered-agent assertions use a distinct never-registered name. Node process state is serialized; WASM modules isolate cases. Temporary string/data/error buffers are owned by try/finally/withAllocs; 43 failure positions verify rollback before any compiled call. Direct tests kclear and dispose clients in finally.
routines.tolerance: No tolerance changes: integer, boolean, type, string and array-shape comparisons preserve exact values/order; numeric fixtures use binary-exact fractions and compare all values with the existing 1e-12 absolute/relative comparator. gnpool output is deliberately not sorted or normalized.

findings.summary: The first full native run exposed a scenario isolation error: two workflows reused additive agent registrations and a supposedly unrelated write triggered a retained watch. CSPICE watches outlive kclear; fresh WASM modules/Python processes hid this.
findings.repair: Give workflows distinct agents/variables and use a permanently unwatched variable before additive registration. Each state sequence is repeatable with retained registration, rather than assuming kclear unregisters agents. Re-run full native parity without retries or weakened observations.

findings.summary: Actual native reads silently truncated fractional indices and wrapped indices above uint32. WASM rejected fractional inputs but wrapped large integral starts into another page. This violates the finite-integer contract and changes the requested data.
findings.repair: Validate nonnegative start and positive room as signed 32-bit integers in both typed adapters before allocation/native conversion. Direct regressions reject fractional, overflowing and nonfinite values for all four readers while preserving valid pool contents.

findings.summary: Actual native reads silently truncated fractional indices and wrapped indices above uint32. WASM rejected fractional inputs but wrapped large integral starts into another page. This violates the finite-integer contract and changes the requested data.
findings.repair: Validate nonnegative start and positive room as signed 32-bit integers in both typed adapters before allocation/native conversion. Direct regressions reject fractional, overflowing and nonfinite values for all four readers while preserving valid pool contents.

findings.summary: A failing-before actual-backend regression showed WASM rejected empty/blank values accepted by native CSPICE and SpiceyPy.
findings.repair: Allow blank strings while validating every value is a string before encoding. Live cases compare every stored string, and direct tests verify leading blanks/padding and post-error recovery.

findings.summary: An actual native pcpool empty-list call failed with SPICE(NULLPOINTER), while WASM/CSPICE no-op semantics preserved the existing variable. SpiceyPy 6.0.3 also cannot express zero count through its pcpool wrapper because max([]) throws before CSPICE.
findings.repair: Keep a non-null dummy row in the native argument buffer while passing original zero element count. In the oracle only for the unrepresentable empty case, invoke SpiceyPy libspice.pcpool_c with n=0 and check_for_spice_error; all nonempty calls use normal sp.pcpool. Compare old numeric type/values before/after zero-count character writes.

findings.summary: Public JSDoc incorrectly claimed empty writes create a size-zero value list. The locked live oracle and both implementations show a no-op preserving an existing variable.
findings.repair: Document actual CSPICE no-op semantics and add live read/type observations before and after zero-count writes, including previous numeric contents before a character write.

findings.summary: WASM iterated plain strings supplied as character/watch arrays, while native correctly rejected non-array inputs. This could mutate pool/watch state using individual characters.
findings.repair: Require actual arrays before validating/encoding character values or watch names; actual-backend boundary tests reject both string arguments before mutation.

findings.repair: Give workflows distinct agents/variables and use a permanently unwatched variable before additive registration. Each state sequence is repeatable with retained registration, rather than assuming kclear unregisters agents. Re-run full native parity without retries or weakened observations.
